newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal PM to visit Pakistan to improve trade ties.
newsitem.headline: Nepal PM to visit Pakistan to improve trade ties.

text.p: Nepal's Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba begins a five-day visit to Pakistan this week during which he will press for softer terms to boost bilateral trade, officials here said on Thursday.
Deuba's visit, beginning on Friday, is the first by a Nepali premier to Pakistan in 13 years.
"We want the volume of our trade to increase," Foreign Ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Bilateral trade totalled 138 million rupees ($2.4 million) last year. Of that, Nepal had a deficit of 132 million rupees ($2.3 million).
Nepali businessmen are seeking more trade information on Pakistan to increase their business share.
"An overland transit route (through India) will facilitate more trade," Padma Jyoti, President of the Federation of the Nepalese Chamber of Commerce and Industries told Reuters.

Nepal and Pakistan, members of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), do not have contiguous borders. Trade between them is routed through Singapore, which is expensive and delays shipments, officials said.
Rajbhandari said Deuba likely would discuss simpler ways to facilitate direct trade. He did not elaborate.
Nepal will also ask for additional tariff concessions available to least developed countries (LDCs) under SAARC's South Asian Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA) provisions, Rajbhandari said.
SAPTA was incorporated within the SAARC framework in 1993 to promote intra-regional trade through tariff concessions and extra incentives to LDCs.
Trade between the seven South Asian nations -- Nepal, Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and the Maldives -- represents only three percent of the global volume.
Officials said Deuba would meet with Pakistani President Farooq Ahmad Khan Leghari and Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.
He also was to visit the southern port city of Karachi, Pakistan's business capital, to invite more investment in the Himalayan kingdom.
Pakistani investors have joint ventures in hotels, textiles and banks in Nepal.
"Nepal will welcome more Pakistani investment," Rajbhandari said.
Foreign investors are provided tax and non-tax incentives including guarantees for repatriation of profits, he said.
